the addition of BMAB can greatly enhance the intermolecular activity of the SDBAS aqueous solution, and that the synergistic interaction of the electrostatic attraction between SDBAS anion and BMAB cation and p p stacking between the benzene ring of BMAB cation with SDBS anion largely increases the SDBS surface concentration, leading to a significant reduction in IFT.
the SDBS can greatly improve its interfacial activity by forming the SDBS–organic salt intermolecular interaction.

the addition of a small amount of organic salt can greatly improve the interfacial properties of anionic surfactants in oil-water systems, and the synergistic mechanism is the electrostatic attraction between the surfactant and salt molecules, which is further enhanced by p p stacking interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the great improvement of the traditional surfactant performance through the additional organic salt, which provides a novel idea for the development of new surfactants.
the great improvement of the interfacially active surfactant via intermolecular interaction.
the synergistic effect of electrostatic attraction and pi-pi stacking interaction, which is expected to greatly promote the application of the traditional anion surfactants in the oil industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of BMAB could greatly improve the interfacial properties and tolerance of SDBS in the brine water/crucde oil system, and this SDBS/BMA system could be used in the EOR process.

the synergistic interaction of the electrostatic attraction with p p stacking interaction between SDBS and BMAB greatly enhanced the interfacial properties of SDBS, and this synergistic effect would provide a new idea for the development of the surfactants in enhanced oil recovery.
the SDBS/ BMAB mixture can be a promising candidate for enhanced oil recovery (EOR).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of a proper organic salt could significantly improve the interfacial performance of the traditional anion surfactant.

the synergistic interaction of electrostatic and p p stacking interactions could greatly increase the surfactant concentration at the interface, leading to the significant reduction of interfacial tension.
the synergistic interaction between the electrostatic and the p p stacking interaction is a novel and efficient method to improve the surfactant performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SDBS and BMAB mixture can be used as a potential low-salt-tolerant and low-temperature-tolerant surfactant system to enhance oil recovery.
the synergistic effects between the electrostatic and p p stacking interactions could be a potential way to improve the surfactant IFT performance in a low concentration.
the addition of BMAB can effectively reduce the IFT of the SDBSBMAB system, which may be a new strategy for enhancing the interfacial performance of the anionic surfactants.
